summary: Music playback no longer silently no-ops and reports success when Discord's voice connection dropped and never reconnected.
details: After a voice websocket drop (Discord close code 1006) whose reconnect stalled or failed, the AudioPlayer thread's own is_playing() state could keep reporting True with no live connection behind it. play() trusted that flag alone to decide 'already playing' and did a live source-swap, which does nothing when there is no real connection to swap into -- the tool call still reported status=ok and Nora's reply claimed playback started while nothing was audible.

play() now also checks is_connected() before taking the crossfade/live-swap path. When the connection is not actually alive, it falls through to a real voice_client.play() call, which -- like discord.py itself -- raises rather than doing nothing, so the failure surfaces as an honest 'unavailable' instead of a false 'ok'.
limitations: This makes the failure visible instead of silent; it does not add automatic reconnection. A dropped voice connection still requires an explicit /music stop + /music play (or a fresh request) to rejoin.
